negative_findings.description: No MK business outlet in this cell was observed to run a dedicated, structured 'people moves / appointments' column analogous to a Western 'Movers & Shakers' rubric. Appointment stories appear as ordinary news items scattered through economy/banking categories.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches across Kapital, Faktor, Sloboden Pecat, Nezavisen, Pari and Bankarstvo returned individual appointment articles but no standing personnel rubric or tag page dedicated to executive moves.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection cannot rely on a single high-yield feed per outlet; A5 must run keyword-filtered crawls over broad economy sections, which raises noise and cost and makes recall dependent on glossary completeness.

negative_findings.description: Three cell-seed outlets — Biznis Vesti (biznisvesti.mk), Fokus (fokus.mk) and Ekonomija i Biznis (ekonomijaibiznis.mk) — did not surface with a confirmed live article URL in any query run in this pass; only encyclopedic/second-hand references appeared for Ekonomija i Biznis.
negative_findings.result_summary: Targeted mk queries naming these domains returned results from other outlets instead. No fetch was attempted, so this is a hypothesis of low search visibility, NOT evidence the sites are dead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: These are named in the coverage cell, so leaving them unresolved would look like coverage that does not exist. They must go to the deterministic liveness pass before being scored as usable.

negative_findings.description: The explicit mk query on banking-sector reorganisation and layoffs returned only regulator and encyclopedic material (NBRM banking-system pages, Wikipedia), not media reporting on redundancies at MK banks.
negative_findings.result_summary: Query 'банкарски сектор Македонија реорганизација отпуштања вработени kapital.mk' produced zero media articles about layoffs or restructuring headcount in the MK banking sector.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Either MK banks genuinely shed staff quietly without media pickup, or the local vocabulary for it differs (e.g. 'технолошки вишок', 'рационализација', 'намалување на бројот на вработени'). Both readings mean the layoff/organisation-change branch of A5 is currently under-instrumented for MK.

negative_findings.description: Albanian-language searching found MK appointment journalism in abundance, but essentially all confirmed examples concerned public institutions and utilities (health fund, electronic-communications agency, municipal enterprise, fire service) rather than commercial banks.
negative_findings.result_summary: No Albanian-language article about a commercial-bank executive appointment in North Macedonia was surfaced in this pass, despite using the correct terms (emërimi, drejtor i ri, drejtor ekzekutiv, bankë).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Suggests MK Albanian-language media cover the political-appointment beat far more than the private banking beat; A5 should therefore not expect the Albanian layer to duplicate bank-CEO coverage, but should use it for state-linked financial institutions and for the Albanian-market retail/fintech angle.

negative_findings.description: No outlet in this cell was observed to expose a documented API, sitemap-based archive index, or explicit RSS endpoint in the results returned.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only human-facing category pages and paginated archives were observed (e.g. portalb.mk/category/maqedoni/page/491/, bankarstvo.mk/category/banki/, slobodenpecat.mk/category/vesti/ekonomija/).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design must assume HTML crawling with pagination handling and per-site parsers; budget accordingly and probe /feed/, /rss, /sitemap.xml on each domain during the technical pass.

coverage_gaps.description: The layoff/restructuring lexicon for MK was not empirically validated — no article using redundancy vocabulary was found, so the working glossary ('отпуштања', 'реорганизација') may simply be the wrong register.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a second lexical probe using alternative MK terms: 'технолошки вишок', 'рационализација на работни места', 'намалување на бројот на вработени', 'реструктуирање', 'затворање на филијали/експозитури', plus sq equivalents 'shkurtime vendesh pune', 'ristrukturim'. Validate each against at least one real article before locking the glossary.

coverage_gaps.description: Turkish-language and Turkey-linked coverage is absent from this cell even though Halkbank AD Skopje and Ziraat are Turkish-owned and their executive appointments (e.g. the Halkbank CEO change observed on Bankarstvo) originate in Turkish parent-group announcements and Turkish business press.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a Turkish-language probe (Halkbank/Ziraat 'Kuzey Makedonya genel müdür atama') and route it to whichever cell owns parent-group sources, so MK media coverage can be cross-dated against the parent's own announcement.

coverage_gaps.description: This cell covers the media/commentary layer only. Every appointment story observed traced back to a National Bank (NBRM) consent decision or a Macedonian Stock Exchange (MSE) issuer announcement — the primary records that media merely report, often days later.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Ensure another cell owns nbrm.mk supervisory-consent publications and mse.mk issuer announcements ('Промени во органите на управување и раководење'); use media as the context/why layer and the primary filings as the fact-of-record, and reconcile the two.

coverage_gaps.description: Two legacy archive domains were discovered (arhiva.emagazin.mk, arkiv.portalb.mk) indicating that historical MK/sq appointment coverage lives on separate hosts from current sites — a historical baseline of executive tenure is achievable but requires distinct crawls.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Schedule a one-off historical crawl of both archive subdomains to reconstruct a multi-year MK bank executive tenure timeline, before the archives are retired.

coverage_gaps.description: Executive names appear in Cyrillic (mk), Latin transliteration (en), and Albanian orthography (sq) with inconsistent spellings, and bank names have changed through mergers/rebrands (e.g. NLB Tutunska Banka to NLB Banka, KB Publikum Invest to KB Invest, Ohridska Banka).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build an alias/transliteration table for both persons and institutions, seeded from the MBA historical-data page and NBRM's bank register, and apply it before deduplicating media mentions — otherwise the same appointment will be counted three times.

coverage_gaps.description: The richest editorial depth in this cell (Kapital magazine, Ekonomija i Biznis) sits in print/PDF products rather than in crawlable article HTML, and LinkedIn — the natural corroborator for individual executive moves — is ToS-blocked for automated collection.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Budget for a Kapital and Ekonomija i Biznis subscription and a PDF/OCR pipeline; treat LinkedIn as a manual, analyst-driven confirmation step only, never as an automated feed.

brief: North Macedonia's business-media layer for banking personnel intelligence is small, concentrated, and unexpectedly well-instrumented at the top: Bankarstvo.mk is a genuine sector-specialist that publishes named board appointments, regulator consents and mandate expiries almost as a matter of record, with Kapital Media Group, Faktor.mk, Pari.com.mk and eMagazin.mk forming a solid second ring that adds interviews, executive profiles and 'why he left' context. Time.mk is the practical entry point for the whole ecosystem, clustering the same appointment across every outlet and doubling as an outlet-discovery mechanism, while Portalb.mk (plus Alsat, Telegrafi's MK vertical and Gazeta KOHA) covers the Albanian-language market that mk-only searching misses — though in this pass that Albanian layer proved far stronger on public-institution appointments than on commercial-bank ones. Two structural weaknesses dominate: no outlet runs a dedicated people-moves rubric, so collection must be keyword-driven over broad economy sections with a validated mk/sq/en alias table; and layoff/restructuring reporting could not be surfaced at all with the assumed vocabulary, leaving the organisation-change branch of A5 the least instrumented part of this cell. Every media appointment story observed ultimately derives from an NBRM consent decision or an MSE issuer filing, so this cell should be operated as the context and biography layer on top of those primary records rather than as the fact-of-record itself.
